items.title: Linux servers & DevOps

CI/CD pipelines through GitHub Actions — build, test, deploy, rollback — triggered on merge without manual SSH.
Systemd services, process supervision, zero-downtime reloads and structured logging to journald.
Active-passive failover with Cloudflare DNS switching, PostgreSQL streaming replication and tested failover drills.
Edge configuration on Cloudflare: TLS termination, WAF rules, rate limits, caching headers and origin certificates.

Third-party integrations (Stripe, PayPal, Twilio, shipping providers, partner APIs) with signed webhook handling and idempotent retries.
Background workers, queues and scheduled jobs for email, PDF generation, reconciliation and heavy processing.

items.title: Database architecture
items.desc: PostgreSQL, MongoDB, MariaDB — design, replication, optimization

detail.summary: We design the database schemas and the operational setup behind them — PostgreSQL, MongoDB or MariaDB — so queries stay fast as data grows and backups actually restore. The goal is a database that is boring in the best way.
whatItIncludes: Schema design with proper normalization, indexes, foreign keys and migration history managed through Prisma, TypeORM or plain SQL migrations.
Replication setups: PostgreSQL streaming replicas, MongoDB replica sets, MariaDB primary-replica, with documented failover procedure.
Backup strategy: automated dumps, point-in-time recovery, offsite storage and scheduled restore drills that prove backups work.
Query optimization: explain plans, missing-index reviews, pagination fixes, N+1 audits on the application side.
Connection pooling with PgBouncer or equivalent, and pool sizing tuned against realistic load.
Role separation: migration user, application user, read-only reporting user — no more shared superuser passwords.
detail.whenYouNeedIt: You need this when queries have started to feel slow under normal load, when a migration looks risky, or when backups exist but nobody is sure they can be restored. Also when you are moving from a single-instance database toward replication for redundancy or reporting.
detail.howWeWork: We read the existing schema and query log first; optimization without data is guesswork. Then we propose the changes in writing, apply them to staging with representative data, and only promote to production after load tests and a restore drill.
detail.outcome: A database that answers queries in predictable time, survives a host failure, and whose backups have been restored at least once outside of an emergency.

items.title: Smart contract audit
items.desc: Security review, vulnerability detection, remediation reports

detail.summary: We review Solidity code the way it should be reviewed — by reading every line, running automated analysis and actually running the contracts against adversarial tests. The output is a written report with severity-ranked findings and concrete fix suggestions.
whatItIncludes: Line-by-line manual review focused on access control, arithmetic, external-call ordering, signature replay and upgrade paths.
Automated static analysis with Slither, Mythril, Aderyn and custom detectors, triaging every finding rather than listing raw output.
Fuzz and invariant testing with Foundry where the contract logic supports it — balances never go negative, total supply is preserved, no unauthorized mint path.
Gas review: unnecessary storage writes, expensive patterns, missing short-circuit checks.
A written report with executive summary, per-finding writeup (severity, impact, location, recommendation) and retest confirmation after fixes land.
A follow-up session to walk the team through the findings and the reasoning behind severity calls.
detail.whenYouNeedIt: You need this before any contract holds real value on mainnet, before a governance vote migrates assets, or after a material change to code that a previous audit covered. It is also the right move when an exchange or launchpad requires an independent review.
detail.howWeWork: We start from the spec and the threat model, not the code. If either is missing we write them first — an audit that skips the spec is worth less than the PDF it is printed on. Fixes are reviewed in a second pass, and the final report states what was retested.
detail.outcome: A signed report you can share with stakeholders and counterparties, a test suite in better shape than when we started, and contracts whose remaining risks are known, named and accepted on purpose.

problem.title: The payments trilemma
problem.body: Merchants who want to accept both crypto and cards usually end up juggling three or four separate gateways, each with its own dashboard, fee structure and settlement schedule. Custodial crypto processors hold funds for days and charge 2–4% before anyone sees the balance; traditional processors don't speak blockchain at all. The result is fragmented accounting, slow settlement and a dependency on platforms that can freeze or reverse payments at any time.

solution.title: One non-custodial gateway
solution.body: GembaPay sits in front of Ethereum, BSC, Polygon, Stripe and PayPal as a single integration. Crypto payments flow directly from customer to merchant through a verified smart contract that keeps 1%; card payments ride Stripe Connect and PayPal Partner rails with the same automated split. No wallet is provisioned for the merchant, no balance is held on the platform, and settlement happens in the same transaction as the payment.

whatWeAre.title: What GembaPay is
items: A non-custodial payment router that connects customer wallets and cards directly to merchant wallets and merchant Stripe or PayPal accounts.
A verified set of on-chain contracts that enforce the 1%/99% split atomically, with source code published on Etherscan, BSCScan and PolygonScan.
A pricing engine that quotes 86+ currencies in real time using Chainlink oracles and lets customers pay in the asset they already hold.
A merchant dashboard with transaction history, invoice generation, webhooks and Stripe Connect or PayPal Partner onboarding in one place.

whatWeAreNot.title: What GembaPay is not
items: Not a custodial wallet — we never hold merchant or customer funds, not even for a block.
Not a crypto exchange — we don't convert currencies, we only route payments to the destination the merchant chose.
Not a reversible card processor — on-chain payments settle final; Stripe and PayPal disputes are handled by Stripe and PayPal.
Not KYC-free for fiat rails — Stripe Connect and PayPal Partner require the same compliance you'd meet anywhere else.

architecture.title: Architecture
paragraphs: GembaPay is split into three layers that never share custody of funds. The smart-contract layer handles settlement on Ethereum, BSC and Polygon — one PaymentGateway contract per chain, verified on-chain and deployed once without proxy upgradability. The API layer, written in Node.js and Express on PostgreSQL with Prisma, stores invoices, merchants and transaction history but never holds balances or signing keys. The React frontend is a stateless client that reads the merchant dashboard and guides customers through payment.

Every transaction path is settlement-in-one-step. A crypto payment calls PaymentGateway.pay() with the invoice ID and amount; the contract pulls the Chainlink price, verifies the amount against the invoice, deducts the 1% platform share and forwards 99% to the merchant — all inside a single call with ReentrancyGuard active. A card payment goes through Stripe Connect in the same logical shape, where Stripe handles the destination transfer and application fee.

The resulting system has no "platform wallet" balance to drain. A full compromise of the GembaPay servers cannot move merchant funds, because the merchant's address is fixed on-chain in the invoice and Stripe settles directly into the merchant's connected account.

security.title: Security

The guiding principle is that GembaPay should fail safely: if the platform goes down, in-flight payments are either confirmed on-chain or they simply never happened, and no merchant balance is at risk either way.

problem.title: No-code crypto tools that still gatekeep
problem.body: Most platforms that advertise "create your own token" hide a shared proxy contract under the hood. Every project they launch shares an upgrade path, an admin key and the platform's reputation, so if the platform disappears or flips a switch, every project inherits the fallout. Independent developers who don't want that dependency are forced back to hand-written Solidity, CLI deployments and manual verification.

solution.title: Your contract, your keys
solution.body: GembaTools deploys a brand-new, standalone contract for every project — ERC20, ERC721, ERC721A or ERC1155 — with source verified automatically after deployment. There is no proxy, no master contract, no delegatecall and no admin role for us to retain. Once deployed, the contract belongs entirely to the wallet that paid the flat creation fee.

whatWeAre.title: What GembaTools is
items: A form-based deployer for independent token and NFT contracts on Ethereum, BSC, Polygon and Base.
A presale page generator that binds a sale to a specific token and deposits raised funds directly to the project wallet.

architecture.title: Architecture
paragraphs: The contract layer is deliberately boring. Seven independent factory contracts live on each supported network; each factory takes constructor arguments from the UI, deploys a standalone child contract and emits a Created event with the new address. Children are not proxies — they are fully self-contained, immutable binaries with their own storage, ownership and ABI.

The frontend is a wagmi/viem React app that reads factory events to populate a user's dashboard, so a wallet always sees the contracts it created even if our backend disappears. Presale, liquidity and trading flows write directly to the child contracts or to Uniswap V3 — the GembaTools backend is a convenience layer, not a custody layer.

Security reviews are part of the development loop. Each factory passes through Slither with zero high-severity findings before it reaches mainnet, and all addresses are published so projects and their auditors can read the exact source before deploying.

security.title: Security

items.label: Contract independence

gembaticket.cardDescription: GembaTicket is a completely free, next-generation online ticketing platform built on web3, blockchain and smart-contract technology, that lets organizers sell tickets online and receive the proceeds in their own balances the moment a purchase is made.
gembaticket.heroIntro: GembaTicket is a completely free, next-generation online ticketing platform built on web3, blockchain and smart-contract technology, that lets organizers sell tickets online and receive the proceeds in their own balances the moment a purchase is made — removing the need for printed paper tickets and box-office queues, giving full control over access to the event's different entrances, and leaving a permanent NFT keepsake in the hands of attendees.

problem.title: Ticketing built on custody and friction
problem.body: Traditional ticketing platforms hold the buyer's money for weeks and release it long after the event, taking 10–15% along the way. GembaTicket is non-custodial and holds zero custody, charging no fees of its own. The only fees come from the payment providers, and they can be brought down to 1%. So organizers can have fresh funds — up to 99% of total turnover — available even during pre-sales.

solution.title: Payment in, ticket out, no custody and no fees in between
solution.body: GembaTicket sells every ticket through GembaPay — fiat or crypto, the organizer's choice. The ticket itself is a database record protected by an HMAC-signed QR code that rotates every 30 seconds and is sent to the buyer's email address. End users access their tickets without needing to create an account on the platform. Those who want a collectible keepsake of the event can mint a multi-page NFT token to their own web3 wallet.

features.title: Key features
features.intro: Designed so organizers run events the way they always did — and Web3 shows up only when someone actively asks for it.

items.title: Dual ticket modes
items.desc: Standard tickets work like any Web2 system — email delivery, rotating QR. The Web3 mode is optional and mints an NFT collectible token directly to the buyer's wallet.

items.title: QR rotation
items.desc: Ticket QR codes are HMAC-signed with a TTL and valid for 30 seconds. A shared screenshot stops validating the moment the 30-second timer rolls over.

items.title: GembaPay-powered checkout
items.desc: Buyers pay in EUR, USD and 51 more fiat currencies, or ETH, BNB, POL, EURC, USDC or USDT. Funds route directly to the organizer's wallet or Stripe/PayPal account, with no platform custody and no platform fees.

items.title: Multi-organizer marketplace
items.desc: A single platform hosts multiple organizers, each with their own events, branding and payout rails. Revenue splits are configured per event.

items.title: Clone-factory contracts
items.desc: Each event deploys a minimal EIP-1167 clone of the ticket template on GembaBlockchain, giving every end user access to take a keepsake of the event.

items.title: Scanner app
items.desc: Door staff use a phone, tablet or any internet-connected scanning device that validates QR codes in real time.

architecture.title: Architecture
paragraphs: GembaTicket splits into three cleanly separated layers. The payments layer is GembaPay, which handles fiat and crypto checkout and settles funds directly to the organizer. The ticketing layer is a Node.js and Express API on PostgreSQL and Redis that stores events, ticket records and rotating QR secrets — it never holds customer funds or private keys.

The on-chain layer runs on GembaBlockchain. Events offer their own smart contract and NFT collectibles — a clone of the ticket contract is deployed via EIP-1167 minimal proxy, keeping deployment cost ~0. Organizers can set up different ticket price tiers (Early Bird, Regular, VIP, Stage — max 10) and timers for when a tier becomes active — by date, when the previous tier sells out, or a combination of both. Different access zones can be set per ticket tier, so attendees enter through different gates. Buyers who mint an NFT pay their own gas ~0 and get a completely free keepsake of their favorite concert; the contract stores the ticket metadata on IPFS and, on mint, transfers ownership directly to the buyer's wallet.

At the door, scanning is entirely Web2. The scanner app sends a signed QR payload and a timestamp to the API; the API validates the signature, checks the ticket is active and returns pass (green) or fail (red) in under 200 ms. Organizers have full control over access to their event — they can have different scanning devices per zone, each scanner knowing exactly which ticket tier to admit and which not. For example: the Regular scanner admits all zones, the VIP scanner only VIP and Stage, the Stage scanner only Stage. Scanners can also be configured for multi-day festivals and conferences — it's all in the organizer's hands.

The organizer has an intuitive interface to manage everything: see stats for sold/remaining tickets and collected revenue, add new tiers or increase the supply of existing ones, and watch in real time how many attendees have passed through the entrance scanners.

Anyone can register as an organizer completely free of charge. The only requirement to start creating events and accepting direct payments to their own balances is to register with the payment provider GembaPay — from there they get an API key and webhook secret, which they add to their account, and the "Create event" button becomes active.

items.title: Concerts and festivals
items.desc: Music events with ticket tiers or without, session tracks, and optional VIP NFT collectibles for attendees who want a lasting keepsake.

items.title: Sports, venues and conferences
items.desc: Recurring events that benefit from rotating QR codes against screenshot fraud and from direct settlement to the organizer's own account.

items.title: Clubs and small parties
items.desc: Organizers who want a pay-link workflow with multi-currency acceptance and minimal fees compared to mainstream platforms.

items.title: Token-gated events
items.desc: Events that restrict entry to holders of a specific NFT, combining on-chain eligibility checks with off-chain ticket delivery.

security.title: Security
security.body: Two categories of risk: funds and tickets. We address funds by never holding them — GembaPay settles every purchase directly to the organizer. No administrative or other hidden fees are charged, no unwanted insurance is added — the customer pays the price they see, and the organizer has access to up to 99% of that amount within seconds! We address tickets by having users receive their ticket seconds after purchase, straight to their pre-verified email — with no risk of loss or an undelivered courier package — and by tying ticket validity to QR codes that rotate, so leaked screenshots lose value within seconds. Tickets are not tied to a name, and you can always gift or resell the ticket you bought.

items.label: Zero custody
items.value: No private keys stored for users, no escrow balance held on the platform. Funds route through GembaPay straight to the organizer.

items.label: QR rotation
items.value: Ticket QR codes are HMAC-signed with a short TTL. A shared screenshot stops validating as soon as the timer rolls.

items.label: Audit posture
items.value: Slither and Mythril audits completed on v2 contracts; no critical findings. All contracts use OpenZeppelin v5 primitives.

items.label: Clone-factory pattern
items.value: EIP-1167 minimal proxies keep the cost of deploying an event at =0 thanks to GembaBlockchain. Organizers and end users never know about it, yet can always inspect the smart-contract code.

educhain.tagline: A safe Web3 sandbox where teachers learn before students do.
educhain.cardDescription: An EU-focused educational platform with role-based access, live leaderboards, an NFT gallery and a structured 16-hour student curriculum plus a 3-day teacher training program.
educhain.heroIntro: EduChain prepares European classrooms for Web3 without putting anyone at financial risk. Everything runs on GembaBlockchain testnet, so students can deploy tokens, mint NFTs and trade safely while teachers manage the whitelist. A dedicated training track certifies educators before they step into the classroom.

problem.title: Web3 curriculum without a safe playground
problem.body: Schools that want to teach blockchain run into two walls. Mainnet is too risky — students can't experiment with real assets, and regulators won't allow minors to touch them anyway. Existing sandboxes are either too abstract, with no real wallets or real deploys, or too technical — Hardhat CLI, testnet faucets and MetaMask for eleven-year-olds — and neither form teaches teachers anything at all.

solution.title: A guided GembaBlockchain testnet classroom
solution.body: EduChain is a full-stack learning environment running on GembaBlockchain testnet, where every student has a real wallet, real gas and real transactions — just without real financial consequences. A teacher-administered whitelist gates access, a built-in faucet funds exercises, and the curriculum walks teachers through a 3-day training program before students touch anything. Structured lessons, live leaderboards and an NFT gallery give educators the instructional scaffolding that general-purpose testnets lack.

whatWeAre.title: What EduChain is
items: A classroom-grade Web3 sandbox running end-to-end on GembaBlockchain testnet, including ERC20 token deployment, ERC721 NFTs and a peer-to-peer marketplace.
A role-based platform with distinct dashboards for students, teachers and administrators, including whitelist management and progress tracking.
A 16-hour structured student curriculum paired with a 3-day teacher training track that certifies educators before they lead students.
A GDPR-aware product designed for European schools, with data minimization and a pedagogical flow reviewed against EU classroom norms.

whatWeAreNot.title: What EduChain is not
items: Not a mainnet platform — nothing students do has financial value, and that is the point.
Not an investment simulator or trading game — the goal is understanding the mechanics, not speculating.
Not a replacement for a teacher — materials guide, but a trained educator runs the session.
Not a general-purpose developer tool — the UX is tuned for a 14-year-old, not for a Solidity engineer.

features.title: Key features
features.intro: Everything a classroom needs to move through a Web3 unit in one semester, with enough structure that a teacher without a CS background can still lead confidently.

items.title: Role-based dashboards
items.desc: Students, teachers and administrators each get a tailored view with the tools and data appropriate to their role.

items.title: Built-in GMB faucet
items.desc: Teachers fund student wallets with GembaBlockchain testnet GMB from a shared pool — no external faucet queues, no lesson interrupted by empty gas tanks.

items.title: ERC20 and NFT workshops
items.desc: Structured exercises that walk students through deploying a token, minting an NFT collection and listing items on a marketplace.

items.title: Live leaderboards
items.desc: Classroom-wide scoreboards reward task completion and quiz performance — useful for gamified units without adding real-money incentives.

items.title: Teacher training track
items.desc: A 3-day program certifies teachers in the platform's pedagogy, the underlying Web3 concepts and classroom-management specifics.

architecture.title: Architecture
paragraphs: The platform runs on six GembaBlockchain testnet contracts written in Solidity 0.8.19 with OpenZeppelin primitives: a Whitelist, a GameToken ERC20, two NFT contracts (one predefined, one custom), a TokenMarketplace and an ETHFaucet. Every contract is a real, deployed artifact on a real network, so students see transaction hashes, gas fees and block confirmations exactly as they would on mainnet.

The frontend is React 18 with ethers.js v5, designed to be usable without previous blockchain exposure. Wallet onboarding is guided step by step, and most classroom actions are wrapped in UI that explains what's happening on-chain in plain language before sending the transaction.

Teachers administer the environment through a dedicated dashboard that controls whitelist entries, faucet allocations, curriculum progress and student reports. EduChain deliberately doesn't integrate with student identity systems or gradebooks — the school retains that data under its own policies, and EduChain only tracks what it needs to teach.

items.title: Secondary schools

items.title: Vocational and technical colleges
items.desc: Foundation-level Web3 training for students moving toward fintech, software and emerging-tech careers.

items.title: Teacher professional development
items.desc: Continuing-education programs for educators who need to teach blockchain but haven't worked with it themselves.

items.title: EU-funded pilots
items.desc: Research projects on digital literacy and emerging technology in classrooms that need a GDPR-aware sandbox to demo in.

atlas.tagline: Unify shift planning, check-in, permits and inventory for industrial teams.
atlas.cardDescription: A modular SaaS platform for refineries, plants and workforce-heavy operations. Swap fragmented spreadsheets and standalone tools for one system, with an optional self-hosted Docker edition.
atlas.heroIntro: Atlas brings shift planning, digital check-in and check-out, inventory, digital permits, an integrated office suite and an AI assistant into one platform built for industrial work. Designed alongside refinery operators, it replaces the usual patchwork of spreadsheets and vendor tools with something teams can actually run end-to-end.

problem.title: Industrial operations stitched together by spreadsheets
problem.body: Walk into a refinery turnaround, a large construction site or a busy plant and you'll see the same thing — shift rosters on a whiteboard, permits on paper, inventory in Excel, check-in on a clipboard. Each vendor tool covers one slice and none of them talk to each other. The people who actually run the work spend more time reconciling spreadsheets than planning the work itself.

solution.title: One modular platform
solution.body: Atlas puts shift planning, check-in and check-out, inventory, digital permits, an integrated office suite and an AI assistant under one roof. Modules activate independently, so an operator can start with scheduling and check-in and add permits, inventory and documents as the team is ready. For clients with strict data-residency requirements, the entire platform runs as a self-hosted Docker deployment on their own infrastructure.

features.title: Key features
features.intro: Designed alongside refinery and plant operators — not in a design studio in a different city — so each module solves a problem somebody has actually been paid to solve.

items.title: Shift planning
items.desc: Rosters with skills, certifications and rest rules. Changes propagate instantly to crew members on mobile.

items.title: Check-in and check-out
items.desc: Badge, QR or biometric entry with timestamps, location and shift context. Attendance rolls up to payroll and access control.

items.title: Digital permits
items.desc: Permit-to-work, hot-work and confined-space permits issued, reviewed and archived on the platform with full audit trail.

items.title: Inventory and parts
items.desc: Tool and consumable tracking, low-stock alerts and issue/return workflows tied to work orders.

items.title: Integrated office
items.desc: Documents, tasks and messaging inside the same platform, so day-to-day coordination doesn't need a separate SaaS stack.

items.title: AI assistant
items.desc: A contextual assistant that answers procedural questions, drafts reports and finds information across the platform's own data.

architecture.title: Architecture
paragraphs: Atlas is a classic modular monolith — React on the frontend, Node.js and PostgreSQL on the backend — packaged so that every module is independently deployable. A client who only needs shift planning and check-in runs a slim subset; a refinery that wants permits, inventory, documents and the AI assistant turns the rest on without migrating data.

Deployment comes in two shapes. The hosted SaaS runs on GEMBA's Hetzner infrastructure with failover and database replication, which is the fastest way for most teams to start. The self-hosted Docker edition bundles the same stack into containers that run on the client's own servers — useful for sites with strict data-residency, offline or security requirements.

The AI assistant is layered on top rather than baked in. It reads what the platform already knows — shift logs, permit history, inventory movements, documents — and answers in context. It doesn't retrain on client data, and it doesn't leave the boundary of the client's installation when self-hosted.

items.title: Refineries and chemical plants
items.desc: Turnaround planning, crew logistics and permit management during high-intensity shutdown and commissioning windows.

items.title: Construction and industrial services
items.desc: Site attendance, tool tracking and document control across distributed crews and subcontractors.

items.title: Workforce-heavy operations
items.desc: Any business where shift-based crews, badges and permits matter more than conference-room software.

items.title: Regulated sites
items.desc: Facilities that require auditable permit history, attendance records and controlled access, with the option to host everything internally.

kotkata.tagline: A hand-drawn NFT collectible gifted to every GembaPay customer.
kotkata.cardDescription: 10,000 unique Sphynx-cat NFTs deployed on Ethereum, BSC and Polygon. Gas-optimized ERC721A contracts, 5% ERC2981 royalties, IPFS-backed metadata, and minting gas as low as $0.001 on Polygon.
kotkata.heroIntro: Kotkata is a generative collection of 10,000 hand-drawn Sphynx cats that doubles as a loyalty program for GembaPay merchants. Each customer who completes a payment can claim a free NFT across three networks. The contract is ERC721A with on-chain royalties, signature-based minting and Slither-clean audits.

problem.title: NFT loyalty without the loyalty
problem.body: Most "free NFT with every purchase" campaigns either charge the user gas on mainnet — which feels like a fee, not a gift — or settle for a giveaway on a chain nobody uses. Gas-heavy mints on Ethereum can cost more than the NFT itself; cheaper chains look disposable. Neither outcome actually makes a customer feel they got something.

solution.title: A gift across three chains
solution.body: Kotkata is a hand-drawn NFT gifted to every GembaPay customer who completes a payment. The same 10,000-piece collection lives on Ethereum, BSC and Polygon, and each merchant's customer can claim on whichever chain makes sense for them. On Polygon, gas for minting is roughly a tenth of a cent — closer to a sticker than an invoice.

features.title: Key features
features.intro: An ERC721A collection designed so the gift experience scales without burning gas, and the art is worth keeping.

items.title: 10,000 hand-drawn pieces
items.desc: A Sphynx-cat collection illustrated in-house, not generated by script. Each piece is an original artwork with its own attributes.

items.title: ERC721A efficiency
items.desc: Azuki's ERC721A reduces bulk-mint gas by up to 70%, keeping claim costs low even when demand spikes.

items.title: Multi-chain deployment
items.desc: The same collection on Ethereum, BSC and Polygon. Customers claim where they already hold assets; the experience is identical on each.

items.title: ERC2981 royalties
items.desc: 5% secondary-sale royalties enforced on-chain through the standard. OpenSea and other marketplaces honor ERC2981 royalty routing.

items.title: Signature-gated minting
items.desc: EIP-712 signed claim tickets let GembaPay distribute NFTs free of charge without exposing a public mint function.

items.title: IPFS-backed metadata
items.desc: Images and metadata store permanently on IPFS through Filebase, so the collection outlives any single frontend or hosting provider.

architecture.title: Architecture
paragraphs: Kotkata is a straightforward ERC721A contract written in Solidity 0.8.27, with 5% royalties via ERC2981 and OpenZeppelin access control. The same source code compiles to three identical deployments on Ethereum, BSC and Polygon; each deployment independently tracks its own supply, so there is no cross-chain state to synchronize.

Claims are signature-gated. When a GembaPay customer qualifies, the backend issues an EIP-712 signature authorizing a specific wallet to mint a specific token ID on a specific chain. The contract verifies the signature, checks the nonce and mints directly to the customer — the platform never holds NFTs in an intermediate wallet.

Media is generated once and served from IPFS through Filebase, with a Sharp-based pipeline producing the fixed image sizes each marketplace expects. All 33 contract tests passed and Slither returned no findings before mainnet deployment across the three networks.

items.title: GembaPay merchant loyalty
items.desc: Every merchant's customers automatically qualify for a Kotkata NFT after completing a GembaPay-processed payment.

items.title: NFT collectors
items.desc: Collectors who value hand-drawn, small-cap Sphynx-cat art with on-chain provenance across three chains.

items.title: First-time NFT recipients
items.desc: Customers who have never held an NFT before get a free one with no gas friction on Polygon — a low-risk introduction.

items.title: Marketing and loyalty campaigns
items.desc: Merchants that use the Kotkata gift as part of seasonal campaigns or customer-milestone rewards.

gembaescrow.tagline: Trustless escrow for property, vehicles and high-value assets — settled in minutes.
gembaescrow.cardDescription: A multi-party escrow platform with buyer, seller, notary and optional agent roles. Funds lock in a dedicated contract deployed via clone factory, released only on notary approval or after the deadline.
gembaescrow.heroIntro: Gemba Escrow replaces traditional escrow accounts with smart contracts you can audit. Buyers deposit once; a licensed notary verifies off-chain, then approves on-chain to distribute funds to seller, agent and notary in a single transaction. If the deadline passes without approval, the buyer reclaims their full deposit.

problem.title: Escrow that takes weeks and costs thousands
problem.body: Traditional escrow for property and high-value assets routes through a bank or specialized escrow agent, costs 1–3% of the transaction value, and takes days or weeks to settle. Smart-contract escrow exists but usually skips the one thing that makes escrow meaningful — the licensed professional who verifies off-chain facts. The result is either slow and expensive, or fast and missing the trust anchor.

solution.title: On-chain settlement, off-chain expertise
solution.body: Gemba Escrow models the full transaction: buyer, seller, licensed notary and optional agent each with a role in the contract. The buyer deposits once; the notary performs the real-world checks they would in any traditional closing, then approves on-chain to release funds in a single transaction. If the deadline passes without approval, the contract automatically returns the buyer's deposit — no court, no paperwork, no custodian in between.

features.title: Key features
features.intro: Every transaction spawns its own contract. Terms, parties and deadlines are fixed at creation and cannot be changed later by anyone — which is the whole point.

items.title: Per-transaction contract
items.desc: A clone-factory pattern deploys a fresh escrow contract for each deal, with buyer, seller, notary and agent addresses fixed at creation.

items.title: Multi-party roles
items.desc: Buyer deposits, seller receives, notary approves, and an optional agent can participate — with capped total fees of 20% across notary and agent.

items.title: Deadline-based refund
items.desc: If approval doesn't happen before the deadline, the buyer reclaims their full deposit automatically on the next transaction. No dispute process required.

items.title: IPFS-linked documents
items.desc: Contracts, identity verifications and property documentation anchor on IPFS, with hashes stored on-chain for provable audit trails.

items.title: Clone-factory efficiency
items.desc: Minimal-proxy deployment keeps per-transaction gas cost low enough to be economically viable even for mid-value deals.

items.title: React 18 + ethers v6
items.desc: A buyer-friendly frontend walks parties through deposit, document signing and approval with full wallet integration.

architecture.title: Architecture
paragraphs: Gemba Escrow uses a factory plus per-deal contract design. The factory contract, written in Solidity 0.8.20 with OpenZeppelin Ownable, deploys a new Escrow clone for every transaction. Each clone locks funds against specific buyer, seller, notary and agent addresses set at construction — those addresses are immutable for the lifetime of the deal.

Settlement is a single function call. Once the notary approves, the contract distributes principal to the seller, capped fees to notary and optional agent, and emits a Settled event. Before approval, only the buyer can trigger a reclaim — and only after the deadline has passed. No party, including GEMBA, has override rights.

Supporting documents live on IPFS. Parties upload identity, property or vehicle paperwork through the frontend; the system stores the hash on-chain and the content on IPFS, so anyone with the hash can verify they have the exact document that was agreed to.

items.title: Real estate
items.desc: Property purchases where buyer, seller and notary need a neutral, auditable settlement path without involving a bank escrow desk.

items.title: Vehicle and high-value asset sales
items.desc: Cars, boats and other registered goods where buyer protection matters but traditional escrow is overkill.

items.title: Cross-border transactions
items.desc: International deals that would otherwise need correspondent banking, moved onto a transparent smart contract instead.

items.title: Commercial agreements
items.desc: Licenses, intellectual property transfers and other deals where a notary's role is about verification, not money movement.

gembawin.tagline: Time-locked bounty payouts with on-chain guarantees for organizers and winners.
gembawin.cardDescription: A bounty and rewards smart contract that locks prize pools in ETH, BNB, USDT or USDC, enforces a 30-day claim window, then returns any unclaimed funds to the organizer.
gembawin.heroIntro: GembaWin takes the trust out of running contests, hackathons and bug bounties. Organizers deposit prizes on-chain across technical and marketing categories, assign winners, and let the contract handle payouts when the deadline hits. Winners have 30 days to claim; anything unclaimed returns cleanly to the organizer.

problem.title: Bounty programs that rely on trust
problem.body: Contests, hackathons and bug bounties usually run on good faith — the organizer promises a prize, the winner delivers, and payment arrives days or weeks later (or not at all). For winners, that lag is frustrating; for organizers, unclaimed prizes are hard to recover without lawyers or paperwork. Both sides want the same thing — a guarantee that doesn't depend on either party showing up at the right time.

solution.title: Prize pools on-chain, rules enforced by contract
solution.body: GembaWin locks a contest's entire prize pool in a smart contract before the contest opens — ETH, BNB, USDT or USDC — and enforces the payout rules automatically. Organizers assign winners across technical and marketing categories; winners claim within a fixed 30-day window and the contract pays out directly to their wallet. Anything still unclaimed after the window returns cleanly to the organizer, no dispute required.

features.title: Key features
features.intro: A small contract doing one thing well — holding prize money honestly until the right moment and returning the remainder cleanly afterward.

items.title: Multi-asset prize pools
items.desc: Prizes funded in native ETH and BNB or in ERC20 stablecoins USDT and USDC, using SafeERC20 for reliable transfers.

items.title: Category-based payouts
items.desc: Organizers split awards across technical and marketing (or other custom) categories, with independent winner lists per category.

items.title: 30-day claim window
items.desc: Winners have exactly 30 days from assignment to claim. The deadline is on-chain — no opaque internal deadline decided by the organizer.

items.title: Automatic reclaim
items.desc: After the window expires, the organizer can recover any unclaimed prize funds in a single transaction, no support ticket or intervention required.

items.title: ReentrancyGuard protected
items.desc: OpenZeppelin ReentrancyGuard wraps all value transfers; claim and reclaim functions are isolated from cross-call attacks.

items.title: Testnet-tested
items.desc: Deployed across GembaBlockchain Testnet with a clean Slither audit before a mainnet cut.

architecture.title: Architecture
paragraphs: GembaWin is a single, focused Solidity contract — the kind of codebase a security reviewer can read end to end in an afternoon. It tracks prize pools as a mapping of contest identifier to category to funded amount, and it tracks winners as a mapping of contest and category to a list of addresses with claim deadlines attached.

The organizer's flow is deposit, assign, wait. Funds deposit into the contract at contest creation; winner assignments lock payout obligations and start the 30-day timer; the contract pays or returns funds based solely on the timer and recorded assignments. There is no admin override, no pausable mechanism that changes outcomes after the fact.

Multi-chain deployment means organizers can run contests in the asset and network most appropriate for their community. The same contract compiles identically on GembaBlockchain Testnet during testing, and can promote to the GembaBlockchain mainnet without code changes.

items.title: Hackathons
items.desc: Event organizers lock prize money up front and commit to on-chain payouts, giving contestants a visible guarantee before they invest weekends of work.

items.title: Contests and giveaways
items.desc: Marketing teams can run campaigns where prize delivery is provably automatic, reducing disputes and support load.

items.title: Bug bounty programs
items.desc: Security programs pay researchers directly in USDC or native tokens, with a predictable on-chain payout path.

items.title: Community rewards
items.desc: DAOs and online communities reward contributions with stablecoin or native-token prize pools that can't be quietly withdrawn later.

nftviewer.tagline: A multi-chain NFT gallery that reads the blockchain when indexers fall short.
nftviewer.cardDescription: A full-stack viewer for wallets and contracts across Ethereum, Polygon, BSC and Sepolia. Moralis-backed with automatic RPC fallback, IPFS gateway resolution and support for interactive HTML NFTs.
nftviewer.heroIntro: NFT Viewer shows what's in a wallet, a contract, or both at once — across four EVM chains. When Moralis is missing data for freshly minted contracts, the backend reads tokenURI directly from the contract and enriches metadata on the fly. A dedicated HTML proxy lets legacy animated NFTs render cleanly inside the gallery.

problem.title: Blockchain gaps where indexers meet reality
problem.body: Every NFT gallery is only as good as its data source. Indexers like Moralis work well for established collections but lag on freshly minted contracts, and IPFS gateways frequently time out or serve stale content. gembasniper.tagline: Snipe new tokens. Skip every honeypot.

gembasniper.heroIntro: Gemba Sniper Bot is GembaIT's professional on-chain sniper for Uniswap V3 and V4. It subscribes directly to factory events over WebSockets, so it detects new pools the moment they exist on-chain, runs each one through a 10-stage honeypot pipeline — including a real $0.03 round-trip on the live pool — and only buys when the token has already proven it can be sold. Positions are then managed with take-profit, stop-loss, timeout and partial-sell exits, plus a 30-minute auto-unstuck recovery loop. Fully non-custodial: the bot never holds your funds or your private keys.

problem.title: Most snipers buy the honeypot
problem.body: "Buy the first token you see" sniper bots happily snipe honeypots and lose on the very first sell. Worse, most managed bots take custody of user funds — you hand over your money and your keys and hope. New-token launches move in seconds, so traders are forced to choose between reacting too slowly by hand or trusting a black-box bot that can rug them just as easily as the token can.

solution.title: Prove sellability before risking size
solution.body: Gemba runs static heuristics, dynamic probes, V4 hook analysis and transfer simulation, and then a real $0.03 buy followed by an immediate sell on the live pool. If the dust can't sell, the real buy never fires. Throughout, the bot is 100% non-custodial: the wallet is generated or imported by the user, the private key is AES-256 encrypted in the browser before it ever leaves the device, and every transaction settles back into the user's own wallet.

whatWeAre.title: What Gemba Sniper Bot is
items: A non-custodial SaaS sniper for newly-launched ERC-20 tokens on Uniswap V3 and V4.
A 10-stage deterministic honeypot pipeline that cannot be skipped — every stage runs in order and streams its verdict to the dashboard in real time.
A per-network engine: independent bot instances on Ethereum, Base and Sepolia, each with its own wallet, position book and WebSocket subscription.
An open-source pipeline you can read end-to-end before trusting it with capital.

whatWeAreNot.title: What Gemba Sniper Bot is not
items: Not custodial — there is no custodial mode anywhere in the service, and there never will be.
Not a fund that holds your money or your keys — the server only ever sees AES-256 ciphertext.
Not a shared treasury or pooled capital — each user has their own wallet and their own position book.
Not a guarantee — sniping new tokens is high-risk; the pipeline reduces but does not eliminate risk, and we publish no win-rates or PnL figures.

items.title: $0.03 micro-test
items.desc: A real round-trip on the live pool, not a simulation. The bot buys a dust amount through the same router the real buy will use and immediately attempts the matching sell — if any leg fails, the real trade aborts.

architecture.title: Architecture
paragraphs: The product is a detect → screen → micro-test → buy → manage → recover pipeline. Detection subscribes over WebSockets to Uniswap V3 PoolCreated and V4 Initialize events on Ethereum, Base and Sepolia; each detection is decoded, screened with static bytecode and proxy/owner/admin checks, probed for delayed-tax and gas-trap behaviour, simulated buy-then-sell against forked state, and finally micro-tested with a real $0.03 round-trip before any real buy is signed.

Three long-running Node processes plus the dashboard make up the system. The engine handles detection, the pipeline and position management with no HTTP listener; the Express API (JWT auth via single-use email OTPs gated by Cloudflare Turnstile) serves the dashboard; the React dashboard streams every pipeline stage over server-sent events. The engine and API never call each other directly — their only contract is a bot_instances Postgres row carrying an is_running flag and a last_heartbeat.

The bot is non-custodial by construction. The wallet is generated or imported by the user, the private key is AES-256 encrypted in the browser before transmission and the server only ever stores ciphertext. Every transaction the bot signs is a transaction by the user's wallet, paid from the user's wallet, settling back into the user's wallet — users can export the encrypted key and withdraw at any time with no involvement from GembaIT.

gembablockchain.heroIntro: GembaBlockchain is a fully transparent, decentralized, permissionless Proof-of-Stake Layer 1 built on Cosmos SDK + Cosmos EVM and CometBFT. Its native coin, Gemba (GMB), is a utility coin — staking, gas and access — not a speculative asset. Anyone with enough stake can validate; anyone can hold and send GMB. The founder holds no special power: reserves never vote and the founder never validates with privilege.

problem.title: Public infrastructure shouldn't depend on one operator
problem.body: Institutions that want to put services on-chain usually face a choice between permissioned chains run by a single vendor — who can decide who participates — and public chains whose economics are driven by speculation and unpredictable fees. Neither is a neutral, durable foundation for public-interest services. Validator sets are capped, governance concentrates, and the token's value detaches from its actual use.

solution.title: A neutral chain owned by its participants
solution.body: GembaBlockchain uses CometBFT BFT Proof-of-Stake for permissionless entry into a large active validator set, EVM compatibility for the entire Solidity/MetaMask ecosystem, and a fixed pre-minted supply so there is zero inflation. Validator rewards come from a pre-minted reserve and real transaction fees, never from new issuance. The result is a sovereign chain whose security budget is tied to adoption, not to printing money.

whatWeAre.title: What GembaBlockchain is
items: A permissionless PoS Layer 1 — bond GMB above the threshold and you validate; no KYC, no whitelist, no privileged validators.
Fully EVM-compatible — Solidity, 0x addresses, MetaMask, Foundry, ethers/viem and standard JSON-RPC all work out of the box.
Fixed-supply and zero-inflation — 100,000,000 GMB minted once at genesis, never again.
A utility chain for institutions and organizations to deliver services — cheaper access, workplace access control, tickets and perks.

whatWeAreNot.title: What GembaBlockchain is not
items: Not built for speculation — the project seeds no liquidity, runs no exchange or DEX, and makes no public token sale.
Not operator-controlled — no central party can decide who participates or change the rules unilaterally.
Not inflationary — there is no minting after genesis and no dynamic-issuance lever.
Not a closed system — it is a public, sovereign chain anyone can build on and validate.

features.intro: Everything a public-interest L1 needs: permissionless validation, EVM tooling, instant finality and a fixed, honest supply.

architecture.title: Architecture
paragraphs: GembaBlockchain is Cosmos EVM (an off-the-shelf, production-used permissionless PoS + EVM stack) plus a thin Gemba layer: two small Go modules — a zero-inflation validator-reward streamer that pays from a pre-minted reserve, and a fee-split that routes part of every fee back into a public reserve — together with the Solidity treasury, governance and application contracts.

Consensus is CometBFT BFT Proof-of-Stake: validators bond GMB, produce blocks with instant finality, and are slashed for objectively-provable faults (double-signing, downtime). The EVM execution layer makes the chain a drop-in target for the entire Ethereum toolchain, while the native coin and staking live in Cosmos modules.

Reserves (public/municipal, foundation, DAO, contingency, validator) are held in non-voting accounts and released only through governance + timelock — there is no admin key that can drain them and no privileged validator that outranks the rest.

security.title: Security & decentralization
security.body: Decentralization is the goal the design binds to mechanisms, not promises: permissionless entry from block zero, no lever to re-close it, and an economic model where attacking the chain costs more than it secures.

items.label: BFT Proof-of-Stake
items.value: CometBFT needs >1/3 of bonded stake to halt and ≥2/3 to forge — and that stake is slashed. The target is cost-to-attack ≥ 3× value secured.

problem.title: Blockchain access control that no one can actually use
problem.body: On-chain credentials are tamper-evident and auditable, but real workplaces can't ask every employee to install a wallet, guard a seed phrase and pay gas. solution.title: Custodial by design, invisible by default

Employees just get an email + password. Because GMB is not a financial instrument and no funds are ever held, custody carries no money-transmitter or licensing burden. Passes are soulbound; issuing is a mint, firing is an issuer-only force-burn — and PII never touches the chain.

items.desc: An operator panel onboards partner companies with an optional free grace period; companies can also self-register.

items.title: Subscription billing
items.desc: Monthly billing through GembaPay; lapsed subscriptions hit a grace period before access stops — never a silent burn.

architecture.title: Architecture
paragraphs: GembaPass pairs a deliberately minimal ERC-1155 contract — GembaAccessPass, soulbound, issuer-only mint and force-burn, one token id per person — with a Node.js + Express + Prisma backend on PostgreSQL and Redis. The contract answers only 'is this credential alive?'; everything human (identity, zones, hours, rights, logs, PINs) lives off-chain, behind row-level tenant isolation.

Issuing a pass generates a branded QR, pins the image and metadata to IPFS, and mints the NFT to the employee's custodial wallet with that metadata as its token URI. At a door, the scanner checks the on-chain isActive state together with off-chain zone rights, access hours, subscription status and an optional PIN, then logs the entry or exit.

Five React frontends (landing, company dashboard, operator dashboard, employee app and scanner PWA) sit behind an Apache reverse proxy with Cloudflare TLS. The platform issuer wallet — the only privileged key — signs all mints and burns; employee keys are never needed for the access flow.

items.title: Companies & SMEs
items.desc: Issue, manage and revoke employee access passes from a single dashboard, with per-zone rights and access hours.

items.title: Public institutions
items.desc: Workplace and facility access on a public, auditable chain, with personal data kept off-chain for GDPR compliance.

items.title: Multi-site organizations
items.desc: Operators onboard many companies (cloud multi-tenant) or deploy a dedicated single-tenant instance on-prem.

items.title: Employees
items.desc: A simple app shows the access pass, lets them set a PIN, and — for the technical — export the wallet to self-custody.

security.title: Security & privacy
security.body: GembaPass is secure by construction: the on-chain layer is anonymous and minimal, the privileged surface is a single issuer key, and all personal data stays off-chain where it can be deleted.

items.label: No PII on-chain
items.value: The chain holds only an address-to-id capability. Identity, movement logs and PINs live in PostgreSQL with per-company row-level security.

items.label: Soulbound passes
items.value: Non-transferable by construction — the only way out of a wallet is an issuer force-burn, so passes can't be shared or sold as tokens.

items.label: Encrypted custody
items.value: Employee private keys are AES-256-GCM encrypted at rest and never decrypted on the access path; the issuer key is the only privileged secret.

items.label: GDPR erasure
items.value: Deleting an employee revokes (burns) the pass on-chain and deletes their identity and logs off-chain.

items.label: Verified contract
items.value: GembaAccessPass follows the GembaBlockchain security standards and is verified on GembaScan.
